demographics.trauma_type: Unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one

Threat.value: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
Being superalert or watchful or on guard
Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame

issues.item: Threat from Strangers: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
issues.explanation: For trauma involving the unexpected death of a loved one, a specific sense of danger from strangers is hard to reconcile unless there is additional trauma history not represented here. The other threat items reflect generalized hypervigilance, but this item implies an interpersonal-danger context that is not supported by the trauma type or by any trigger, memory, appraisal, or strategy items.

issues.item: Scanning for Danger: I constantly scan my surroundings for signs of danger
issues.explanation: For trauma involving the unexpected death of a loved one, this threat profile is hard to reconcile clinically: all selected items imply persistent fear of immediate external physical danger, which fits assault/combat more than bereavement trauma. In isolation, bereavement-related PTSD can involve arousal, but a purely danger-scanning threat node without any accompanying memory, trigger, appraisal, or strategy content linking the threat to reminders of the loved one's death is not coherent here. This is also difficult to square with the formulation, which specifies no active edges; the threat items strongly imply linkage to triggers or trauma reminders, yet no such connected content is present.

vignette: Samantha is a 31-year-old South Eastern Asian woman who recently sought help for her overwhelming feelings following the unexpected death of her sister. Samantha had always been fiercely independent and driven in her work as a journalist, but since her sister’s passing, she has found it increasingly difficult to focus on anything other than her own heightened sense of threat. Samantha vividly recalls the day she received the news about her sister's sudden death from an accidental overdose. She was at home, working on a story when she got a call from her mother. The shock and disbelief were overwhelming. In the days that followed, Samantha found herself struggling to find solace in anything around her. Even though she knew logically that there was no immediate danger, she could not relax. She would sit for hours with her muscles tense, constantly scanning her environment as if waiting for something worse to happen. Her hypervigilance has become a persistent feature of her daily life. While at work, she is always the first to notice any unusual movements or sounds in the newsroom. Her colleagues have noticed this change and often remark on how alert she seems during meetings. Despite their concern, Samantha cannot seem to shake off this heightened state of awareness. She has come to believe that if she lets her guard down even for a moment, something terrible might happen again. The death of her sister also triggered strong negative emotions in Samantha, which have been overwhelming and difficult to manage. Fear is a constant companion; she fears not only for her own safety but also for the well-being of others close to her. She is haunted by guilt over not being able to prevent what happened to her sister. These feelings are exacerbated when she sees reminders of her sister in their shared surroundings, such as photos or mementos that still adorn her home. Samantha's inability to relax and her constant state of hypervigilance have had significant impacts on her work and personal life. Her concentration at the office has noticeably diminished, leading to missed deadlines and a general sense of frustration. She often finds herself re-reading articles multiple times because she is worried about overlooking critical details or making mistakes. In her personal life, Samantha's relationships have suffered as well. Her ex-husband noticed changes in her behavior early on but did not understand the depth of her emotional turmoil until he heard her express her fears and guilt over dinner one evening. Her friends have also observed that she seems more withdrawn and less engaged during social gatherings. Samantha’s life has been a series of heightened senses and overwhelming emotions since her sister's death, and it is this persistent state that finally brought her to seek help. What frightened her most was the realization that these feelings were not subsiding over time but were instead becoming an ingrained part of her daily experience. She hopes that therapy will provide her with tools to manage her hypervigilance and negative emotions so she can regain a sense of peace in her life.
